title: Chikungunya: acute, subacute and chronic (WHO)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Fever with disabling polyarthralgia. Acute phase: fluids, paracetamol or metamizole, and no NSAIDs or steroids until dengue is excluded. Confirmed chikungunya with persistent arthritis: NSAIDs, then a short low-dose steroid course for severe post-acute disease; chronic inflammatory arthritis beyond 3 months needs rheumatology and DMARDs (usually methotrexate).

sections.title: Recognise
items: Abrupt fever with severe, often incapacitating, symmetrical polyarthralgia of the hands, wrists and ankles, with joint swelling, myalgia, headache, fatigue and rash, usually 4 to 8 days after the mosquito bite.
Phases used by most guidelines: acute (first 3 weeks), post-acute or subacute (3 weeks to 3 months) and chronic (beyond 3 months). Joint pain may last weeks, months or years.
Dengue co-circulates and cannot be excluded clinically early on: manage suspected chikungunya as dengue (including watching for warning signs) until dengue is ruled out.

Severe or atypical disease is most likely in neonates infected around delivery and in older people with comorbidity: encephalitis, myocarditis, hepatitis, AKI, bullous skin lesions. Hospitalisation is a clinical decision (WHO 2025).
Myocarditis and cardiac insufficiency are relatively common in severe chikungunya in infants and older adults, making iatrogenic pulmonary oedema more likely with IV fluids.

sections.title: Investigations
items: RT-PCR for CHIKV RNA in the first week; IgM (ELISA or RDT) from the end of the first week, detectable for about 2 months. IgM cross-reacts with other alphaviruses such as Mayaro and O'nyong-nyong.
Test for dengue (NS1 or PCR, then IgM) and malaria where endemic, with a CBC, because management differs.
Persistent arthritis: ESR, CRP, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP and imaging to exclude rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthritis and other causes before labelling chronic chikungunya arthritis.

sections.title: Acute phase (first 3 weeks)
items: No antiviral exists. Rest, protocolised oral fluids, cold compresses and gentle mobilisation. Avoid mosquito exposure during the first week to prevent local transmission.

Paracetamol: adults over 50 kg 500 mg to 1 g every 4 to 6 hours (maximum 4 g/day); children 10 to 15 mg/kg every 4 to 6 hours (maximum 60 mg/kg/day). Metamizole is an alternative where licensed (WHO and PAHO).
No NSAIDs or aspirin while dengue has not been excluded (WHO strong recommendation). In confirmed chikungunya, WHO allows NSAIDs to be considered for arthralgia and inflammation.
No corticosteroids in acute non-severe disease (WHO 2025).
Uncontrolled pain in adults: add tramadol 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours (maximum 400 mg/day), alone or with paracetamol.

sections.title: Post-acute phase (3 weeks to 3 months)
items: NSAIDs are first-line for persistent joint pain once dengue is excluded (for example ibuprofen 400 to 600 mg 3 times daily, maximum 2.4 g/day, or naproxen 500 mg twice daily), with gastroprotection where indicated, plus physiotherapy (CDC).
Severe polyarthritis or tenosynovitis not controlled by NSAIDs: short course of oral prednisolone, usually 10 to 20 mg/day (up to 0.5 mg/kg/day in severe cases), tapered and limited to about 4 weeks.
Localised synovitis, tenosynovitis or bursitis: topical or local corticosteroid injection (CDC includes topical corticosteroids).
Neuropathic pain features: consider amitriptyline, gabapentin or pregabalin at standard neuropathic doses.

sections.title: Chronic phase (beyond 3 months)
items: Separate chronic inflammatory arthritis (synovitis, raised CRP) from non-inflammatory musculoskeletal pain; refer persistent inflammatory arthritis to rheumatology.

DMARDs for chronic inflammatory arthritis: methotrexate is first-line in most guidelines, hydroxychloroquine for milder disease, and sulfasalazine in combination; use rheumatoid arthritis regimens with standard monitoring.
Continue NSAIDs, physiotherapy and rehabilitation; short steroid courses only for flares. Screen for fatigue and depression, which are common.

sections.title: Severe (hospitalised) disease
items: If IV fluid is needed, use crystalloid rather than colloid, guided by capillary refill time and lactate; give smaller volumes with frequent reassessment in infants, older adults and suspected myocarditis.
No systemic corticosteroids or immunoglobulins for severe arboviral disease, and no prophylactic platelets for counts below 50,000/microlitre without bleeding (WHO 2025).
Echocardiography and ECG for suspected myocarditis; manage encephalitis, AKI and hepatitis supportively.

sections.title: Pregnancy, neonates and national policy
items: Pregnancy: paracetamol at the lowest effective dose; avoid NSAIDs (ductus arteriosus closure, fetal renal injury); metamizole is contraindicated in the third trimester. Refer for obstetric monitoring.
Maternal infection around delivery can cause severe neonatal disease; observe neonates born to viraemic mothers in hospital (several guidelines advise about 7 days).
Avoid NSAIDs in infants under 3 months and codeine in children under 12 years.
India: the NCVBDC 2023 guideline uses the same phased approach with a fixed prednisolone taper and hydroxychloroquine as the main chronic-phase DMARD; this protocol follows WHO 2025, PAHO and CDC.

sections.title: Prevention
items: Mosquito bite avoidance (repellent, covering clothing, screened or air-conditioned rooms) and community Aedes control.

A virus-like particle vaccine (Vimkunya) is licensed in the US, EU and UK and may be considered for higher-risk travellers. The US licence for the live attenuated vaccine (Ixchiq) was suspended in August 2025 over serious adverse events; follow national advice.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving NSAIDs or aspirin before dengue is excluded.
Steroids in the acute phase, or long steroid courses in the post-acute phase.
Labelling chronic arthritis as post-chikungunya on IgM alone without excluding rheumatoid arthritis or gout.
Fluid boluses without reassessment in infants and older adults with possible myocarditis.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: Adults over 50 kg 500 mg to 1 g every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 4 g/day; children 10 to 15 mg/kg every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 60 mg/kg/day
drugs.notes: First line in the acute phase and in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Metamizole (dipyrone)
drugs.dose: Adults 500 mg to 1 g per dose (maximum 4 g/day); children 10 mg/kg per dose up to 4 times daily
drugs.notes: Alternative where licensed. Agranulocytosis; not in the third trimester.

drugs.name: Tramadol
drugs.dose: Adults 50 to 100 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 400 mg/day
drugs.notes: Uncontrolled pain in adults. Not in children under 12 years.

drugs.name: Ibuprofen
drugs.dose: Adults 400 to 600 mg orally 3 times daily with food, maximum 2.4 g/day
drugs.notes: Only after dengue is excluded; confirmed chikungunya with persistent arthralgia.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.dose: Usually 10 to 20 mg/day orally (up to 0.5 mg/kg/day in severe cases), tapered, total about 4 weeks or less
drugs.notes: Post-acute severe polyarthritis or tenosynovitis despite NSAIDs. Not in the acute phase.

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.dose: 7.5 mg orally once weekly, increased as needed to a maximum of 25 mg once weekly, with folic acid
drugs.notes: Chronic inflammatory arthritis under rheumatology; monitor FBC, liver and renal function.

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.dose: 200 to 400 mg orally daily (not above 5 mg/kg/day actual body weight)
drugs.notes: Milder chronic inflammatory arthritis or in combination; retinal screening with long-term use.
